findings.text: The retrieved evidence supports repeated Vandalism hypotheses from the surveillance-event model across multiple windows in three persistent segments (f5-f6, f8-f10, f13-f17). The available evidence is consistent with repeated model activity, but the evidence does not establish that vandalism occurred.

The evidence indicates knife object detections temporally coincided with Vandalism hypotheses in f14, f16 and f17. This is source agreement only and the evidence does not establish involvement or causation.
The retrieved evidence supports train detections coinciding with a Vandalism hypothesis in f2 followed by a Shooting hypothesis in f3. Temporal co-occurrence does not indicate causation.

The evidence indicates single person detections coincided with an Abuse hypothesis in f7 and an Explosion hypothesis in f22. The available evidence does not suggest the detected persons were involved.

The surveillance-event model produced additional hypotheses including Explosion in f0, f18 and f19, Shooting in f1 and f11, Arrest in f4, and RoadAccidents in f12, with listed generic actions and no object detections in those windows. The evidence does not establish that the hypothesized events occurred.

The available evidence suggests the Vandalism-hypothesis segment in f8-f10 occurred before the Shooting and RoadAccidents hypotheses in f11-f12, which occurred before the Vandalism-hypothesis segment starting at f13. The evidence indicates f20 showed a Vandalism hypothesis followed by Explosion hypotheses in f21 and f22, not a strict alternation. All cited windows belong to the same incident anomaly/Vandalism/Vandalism001_x264.mp4:i0.
